source.text: Μετὰ δὲ τὸ παύσασθαι τὸν θόρυβον μεταπεμψάμενος ὁ Παῦλος τοὺς μαθητὰς καὶ παρακαλέσας, ἀσπασάμενος ἐξῆλθεν πορεύεσθαι εἰς Μακεδονίαν.

records.literal_gloss: After now the to have ceased the uproar having sent for the Paul the disciples and having encouraged [them], having said farewell he went out to go to Macedonia.

en.L: Now after the uproar had ceased, Paul, having sent for the disciples and encouraged [them], said farewell and departed to go to Macedonia.
en.B: When the uproar had died down, Paul sent for the disciples and encouraged them. Then he said goodbye and set out for Macedonia.
en.R: After the riot in Ephesus was over, Paul called the followers of Jesus together and encouraged them. Then he said goodbye to them and left for Macedonia.

es.L: Y después de cesar el alboroto, Pablo mandó llamar a los discípulos y, tras animar[los], se despidió y salió para ir a Macedonia.
es.B: Cuando se calmó el alboroto, Pablo mandó llamar a los discípulos y los animó. Luego se despidió y partió hacia Macedonia.
es.R: Cuando terminó el disturbio en Éfeso, Pablo reunió a los discípulos y los animó. Después se despidió de ellos y se fue a Macedonia.

fr.L: Or, après que le tumulte eut cessé, Paul, ayant fait venir les disciples et [les] ayant encouragés, prit congé et partit pour aller en Macédoine.
fr.B: Quand le tumulte se fut apaisé, Paul fit venir les disciples et les encouragea. Puis il leur dit adieu et partit pour la Macédoine.
fr.R: Après l’émeute d’Éphèse, Paul a réuni ceux qui suivaient Jésus et il les a encouragés. Puis il leur a dit au revoir, et il est parti pour la Macédoine.

sw.L: Basi baada ya ghasia kukoma, Paulo, akiwa amewaita wanafunzi na kuwatia moyo, aliagana nao, akaondoka kwenda Makedonia.
sw.B: Ghasia zilipokwisha, Paulo aliwaita wanafunzi, akawatia moyo. Kisha akawaaga, akaondoka kwenda Makedonia.
sw.R: Baada ya fujo kule Efeso kumalizika, Paulo aliwaita pamoja wanafunzi wa Yesu, akawatia moyo. Kisha akawaaga, akaondoka kwenda Makedonia.

decisions.choice: the uproar: the riot in the theater at Ephesus
decisions.reason: The same word is used of the riot in 19:23-41 (19:23 calls it a great disturbance). Paul had already planned to go through Macedonia (19:21).

decisions.choice: encouraged: urged and strengthened them
decisions.reason: The verb covers urging, encouraging and comforting. Here, at a parting, it means strengthening them to go on (as in 14:22, 16:40).

decisions.choice: the riot in Ephesus
decisions.reason: Readable names the event, which the reader met in chapter 19.

decisions.choice: the followers of Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly who the disciples are.

decisions.choice: discípulos at every level
decisions.reason: The book-wide Spanish term: Readable keeps "discípulos" where the English Readable says "followers of Jesus", as in the Gospels; it covers 20:30.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R), also where Luke says "we" ("nous partîmes", "nous sommes partis")
decisions.reason: As in the rest of Acts: the passé simple is the tense of written narrative and suits a public reading; Readable uses the passé composé. The first-person passages from 20:5 keep the same tenses, since Luke is still telling the story, not speaking to the reader. Paul's speech (20:18-35) uses the tenses of speech at every level. This holds for the whole chapter.

decisions.choice: wanafunzi wa Yesu
decisions.reason: Swahili keeps "wanafunzi" (disciples) at every level, as in the rest of Acts; Readable adds "wa Yesu" to make clear whose disciples they are, where the English Readable says "followers of Jesus".

source.text: διελθὼν δὲ τὰ μέρη ἐκεῖνα καὶ παρακαλέσας αὐτοὺς λόγῳ πολλῷ ἦλθεν εἰς τὴν Ἑλλάδα ποιήσας τε μῆνας τρεῖς· γενομένης ἐπιβουλῆς αὐτῷ ὑπὸ τῶν Ἰουδαίων μέλλοντι ἀνάγεσθαι εἰς τὴν Συρίαν ἐγένετο γνώμης τοῦ ὑποστρέφειν διὰ Μακεδονίας.

records.literal_gloss: Having gone through then the regions those and having encouraged them with word much he came into the Greece, \v 3 having spent and months three, having been made a plot against him by the Jews being about to set sail into the Syria, there came [to be] a decision of the to return through Macedonia.

en.L: And having gone through those regions and encouraged them with many words, he came into Greece; \v 3 and having spent three months [there], when a plot was made against him by the Jews as he was about to set sail for Syria, he resolved to return through Macedonia.
en.B: He went through those parts, speaking at length to the disciples to encourage them, and came to Greece. \v 3 He stayed there three months. Just as he was about to sail for Syria, the Jews laid a plot against him, so he made up his mind to go back through Macedonia.
en.R: He went through that area and spoke many times to the believers there to make them strong. Then he went to Greece. \v 3 He stayed there for three months. He was getting ready to sail to Syria, but he learned that some of the Jews had made a plan to attack him. So he decided to go back the way he had come, through Macedonia.

es.L: Y habiendo recorrido aquellas regiones y habiéndolos animado con mucha palabra, llegó a Grecia; \v 3 y después de pasar [allí] tres meses, como los judíos tramaron un complot contra él cuando estaba a punto de embarcarse hacia Siria, tomó la decisión de regresar por Macedonia.
es.B: Recorrió aquellas regiones, animando a los discípulos con muchas palabras, y llegó a Grecia. \v 3 Allí se quedó tres meses. Cuando estaba a punto de embarcarse hacia Siria, los judíos tramaron un complot contra él, así que decidió regresar por Macedonia.
es.R: Pasó por toda aquella región y habló muchas veces a los creyentes de allí para fortalecerlos. Luego fue a Grecia. \v 3 Allí se quedó tres meses. Se estaba preparando para viajar en barco a Siria, pero se enteró de que algunos judíos habían hecho planes para atacarlo. Por eso decidió volver por el mismo camino, a través de Macedonia.

fr.L: Et ayant traversé ces régions et les ayant encouragés par beaucoup de paroles, il vint en Grèce ; \v 3 et ayant passé trois mois [là-bas], comme un complot fut formé contre lui par les Juifs alors qu’il allait s’embarquer pour la Syrie, il prit la décision de revenir par la Macédoine.
fr.B: Il parcourut ces régions, adressant de longs discours aux disciples pour les encourager, puis il arriva en Grèce. \v 3 Il y resta trois mois. Au moment où il allait s’embarquer pour la Syrie, les Juifs formèrent un complot contre lui ; il résolut donc de repasser par la Macédoine.
fr.R: Il a traversé cette région et il a souvent parlé aux croyants pour les rendre forts. Puis il est allé en Grèce. \v 3 Il y est resté trois mois. Il se préparait à partir en bateau pour la Syrie, mais il a appris que des Juifs avaient fait le projet de l’attaquer. Alors il a décidé de revenir par le chemin qu’il avait pris à l’aller, en passant par la Macédoine.

sw.L: Na akiisha kupita katika sehemu zile na kuwatia moyo kwa maneno mengi, alifika Ugiriki; \v 3 na akiisha kukaa [huko] miezi mitatu, Wayahudi walipomfanyia njama alipokuwa karibu kusafiri kwa meli kwenda Siria, aliamua kurudi kupitia Makedonia.
sw.B: Alipita katika sehemu zile, akawatia moyo wanafunzi kwa maneno mengi, kisha akafika Ugiriki. \v 3 Alikaa huko miezi mitatu. Alipokuwa karibu kusafiri kwa meli kwenda Siria, Wayahudi walimfanyia njama, kwa hiyo akaamua kurudi kupitia Makedonia.
sw.R: Alipita katika eneo lile, akazungumza mara nyingi na waumini wa huko ili kuwaimarisha. Kisha akaenda Ugiriki. \v 3 Alikaa huko miezi mitatu. Alikuwa akijiandaa kusafiri kwa meli kwenda Siria, lakini akagundua kwamba baadhi ya Wayahudi walikuwa wamepanga kumshambulia. Kwa hiyo akaamua kurudi kwa njia aliyojia, kupitia Makedonia.

decisions.choice: Greece: southern Greece, the Roman province of Achaia, where Corinth lay
decisions.reason: Macedonia was the northern province. Paul had worked in Achaia before (18:1, 18:12, 18:27).

decisions.choice: a plot by the Jews: a plan to harm him, timed to his sailing
decisions.reason: The word means a secret plan against someone (9:24, 23:30). Luke ties it to the voyage, and the plot makes Paul change his route.

decisions.choice: there came to be a decision: he made up his mind
decisions.reason: The phrase means that a resolve was formed. Paul is the one who changes plan.

decisions.choice: the disciples / the believers there
decisions.reason: "Them" means the disciples in those regions; Balanced and Readable say so.

decisions.choice: he learned that; the way he had come
decisions.reason: Readable adds that Paul found out about the plot and that Macedonia was the road he had come by (20:1). Both follow from the story.

decisions.choice: Ugiriki; Siria
decisions.reason: The usual modern Swahili names for Greece and Syria; "Siria" as in Luke 2:2.

source.text: συνείπετο δὲ αὐτῷ Σώπατρος Πύρρου Βεροιαῖος, Θεσσαλονικέων δὲ Ἀρίσταρχος καὶ Σεκοῦνδος, καὶ Γάϊος Δερβαῖος καὶ Τιμόθεος, Ἀσιανοὶ δὲ Τυχικὸς καὶ Τρόφιμος·

records.literal_gloss: Accompanied then him Sopater of Pyrrhus a Berean, of Thessalonians and Aristarchus and Secundus, and Gaius a Derbean and Timothy, Asians and Tychicus and Trophimus.

en.L: And Sopater [son] of Pyrrhus, a Berean, accompanied him, and of the Thessalonians, Aristarchus and Secundus, and Gaius of Derbe, and Timothy, and [men] of Asia, Tychicus and Trophimus.
en.B: He was accompanied by Sopater son of Pyrrhus from Berea, Aristarchus and Secundus from Thessalonica, Gaius of Derbe, Timothy, and Tychicus and Trophimus from the province of Asia.
en.R: Several men traveled with Paul. They were Sopater son of Pyrrhus, from the city of Berea; Aristarchus and Secundus, from Thessalonica; Gaius, from Derbe; Timothy; and Tychicus and Trophimus, from the province of Asia.

es.L: Y lo acompañaba Sópater [hijo] de Pirro, de Berea; y de los tesalonicenses, Aristarco y Segundo; y Gayo de Derbe, y Timoteo; y de Asia, Tíquico y Trófimo.
es.B: Lo acompañaban Sópater, hijo de Pirro, de Berea; Aristarco y Segundo, de Tesalónica; Gayo, de Derbe; Timoteo; y Tíquico y Trófimo, de la provincia de Asia.
es.R: Varios hombres viajaban con Pablo. Eran Sópater, hijo de Pirro, de la ciudad de Berea; Aristarco y Segundo, de Tesalónica; Gayo, de Derbe; Timoteo; y Tíquico y Trófimo, de la provincia de Asia.

fr.L: Et Sopater [fils] de Pyrrhus, de Bérée, l’accompagnait, et, des Thessaloniciens, Aristarque et Second, et Gaïus de Derbé, et Timothée, et, [des hommes] d’Asie, Tychique et Trophime.
fr.B: Il était accompagné de Sopater, fils de Pyrrhus, de Bérée, d’Aristarque et de Second, de Thessalonique, de Gaïus de Derbé, de Timothée, ainsi que de Tychique et de Trophime, de la province d’Asie.
fr.R: Plusieurs hommes voyageaient avec Paul. C’étaient Sopater, fils de Pyrrhus, de la ville de Bérée ; Aristarque et Second, de Thessalonique ; Gaïus, de Derbé ; Timothée ; et Tychique et Trophime, de la province d’Asie.

sw.L: Na Sopatro [mwana] wa Piro, wa Beroya, alifuatana naye, na kati ya Wathesalonike, Aristarko na Sekundo, na Gayo wa Derbe, na Timotheo, na kati ya [watu] wa Asia, Tikiko na Trofimo.
sw.B: Waliofuatana naye ni Sopatro mwana wa Piro, wa Beroya; Aristarko na Sekundo wa Thesalonike; Gayo wa Derbe; Timotheo; na Tikiko na Trofimo wa jimbo la Asia.
sw.R: Watu kadhaa walisafiri pamoja na Paulo. Nao ni Sopatro mwana wa Piro, kutoka mji wa Beroya; Aristarko na Sekundo, kutoka Thesalonike; Gayo, kutoka Derbe; Timotheo; na Tikiko na Trofimo, kutoka jimbo la Asia.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "Sopater of Pyrrhus", with no "as far as Asia"
alternatives: many later manuscripts leave out "of Pyrrhus"
many manuscripts add "as far as Asia" after "accompanied him"
decisions.reason: The name of Sopater's father is in the early manuscripts and missing from many later ones. Many manuscripts also say these men went with Paul "as far as Asia", which does not fit 20:5-6 well. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: men from the churches Paul had founded, traveling with him to Jerusalem
alternatives: a group with no stated purpose
decisions.reason: Paul's letters speak of a gift for the poor in Jerusalem gathered from the churches of Macedonia, Achaia and Galatia, to be taken by men the churches chose (Romans 15:25-26; 1 Corinthians 16:1-4; 2 Corinthians 8:19-23). In 24:17 Paul says he came bringing gifts. Luke does not say here that these men carried it.

decisions.choice: Gaius of Derbe: another Gaius than the Macedonian of 19:29
decisions.reason: Gaius was a common name. This one is from Derbe in Galatia (14:20).

decisions.choice: Several men traveled with Paul.
decisions.reason: Readable introduces the list with a short sentence of its own.

decisions.choice: Second, Tychique, Trophime
decisions.reason: The usual French forms of the names, as for Aristarque and Timothée; Sopater and Pyrrhus keep the Greek form, which French also uses.

decisions.choice: Sopatro, Piro, Aristarko, Sekundo, Tikiko, Trofimo
decisions.reason: Names in the Swahili form of the other names in Acts (Gayo, Timotheo, Beroya, Thesalonike): the Greek ending dropped and a final vowel kept.

source.text: οὗτοι δὲ προσελθόντες ἔμενον ἡμᾶς ἐν Τρῳάδι·

records.literal_gloss: These and having gone ahead were waiting for us in Troas.

en.L: And these, having gone ahead, were waiting for us in Troas.
en.B: These men went on ahead and waited for us at Troas.
en.R: They went on ahead of us and waited for us in the city of Troas.

es.L: Y estos, habiéndose adelantado, nos esperaban en Troas.
es.B: Estos se adelantaron y nos esperaron en Troas.
es.R: Ellos se fueron antes que nosotros y nos esperaron en la ciudad de Troas.

fr.L: Et ceux-ci, étant partis en avant, nous attendaient à Troas.
fr.B: Ces hommes partirent devant et nous attendirent à Troas.
fr.R: Ils sont partis avant nous, et ils nous ont attendus dans la ville de Troas.

sw.L: Na hawa, wakiisha kutangulia, walikuwa wakitungoja katika Troa.
sw.B: Watu hao walitangulia, wakatungoja Troa.
sw.R: Wao walitutangulia, wakatusubiri katika mji wa Troa.

decisions.choice: us: the narrator includes himself in the group
alternatives: the narrator copies someone else's account
decisions.reason: The first person plural was last used at Philippi (16:10-17). It returns here, as Paul passes through Philippi again (20:6), and runs to 21:18. The text does not say who the narrator is.

decisions.choice: these: probably the whole group of 20:4
alternatives: only Tychicus and Trophimus, the last named
decisions.reason: "These" could point back to the last two names, but most naturally takes in the whole list.

decisions.choice: the city of Troas
decisions.reason: Readable says what Troas is, as at 16:8.

source.text: ἡμεῖς δὲ ἐξεπλεύσαμεν μετὰ τὰς ἡμέρας τῶν ἀζύμων ἀπὸ Φιλίππων, καὶ ἤλθομεν πρὸς αὐτοὺς εἰς τὴν Τρῳάδα ἄχρι ἡμερῶν πέντε, οὗ διετρίψαμεν ἡμέρας ἑπτά.

records.literal_gloss: We then sailed away after the days of the Unleavened [Bread] from Philippi and came to them at Troas within days five, where we stayed days seven.

en.L: But we sailed away from Philippi after the days of Unleavened Bread, and came to them at Troas within five days, where we stayed seven days.
en.B: We ourselves sailed from Philippi after the days of Unleavened Bread, and five days later we joined them at Troas. We spent seven days there.
en.R: We sailed from Philippi after the Jewish Festival of Unleavened Bread. Five days later we met the others in Troas, and we stayed there for a week.

es.L: Pero nosotros zarpamos de Filipos después de los días de los Ázimos, y llegamos adonde ellos estaban, a Troas, en cinco días, donde nos quedamos siete días.
es.B: Nosotros, por nuestra parte, zarpamos de Filipos después de los días de la fiesta de los Panes sin Levadura, y cinco días después nos reunimos con ellos en Troas. Allí pasamos siete días.
es.R: Nosotros salimos en barco de Filipos después de la fiesta judía de los Panes sin Levadura. Cinco días más tarde nos encontramos con los demás en Troas, y nos quedamos allí una semana.

fr.L: Mais nous, nous partîmes par mer de Philippes après les jours des Pains sans levain, et nous vînmes vers eux à Troas en cinq jours, où nous restâmes sept jours.
fr.B: Quant à nous, nous embarquâmes à Philippes après les jours des Pains sans levain, et cinq jours plus tard nous les rejoignîmes à Troas. Nous y passâmes sept jours.
fr.R: Nous sommes partis en bateau de Philippes après la fête juive des Pains sans levain. Cinq jours plus tard, nous avons retrouvé les autres à Troas, et nous sommes restés là une semaine.

sw.L: Lakini sisi tuling'oa nanga kutoka Filipi baada ya siku za [Sikukuu ya] Mikate Isiyotiwa Chachu, na tukawafikia huko Troa katika siku tano, mahali tulipokaa siku saba.
sw.B: Sisi tuliondoka Filipi kwa meli baada ya siku za Sikukuu ya Mikate Isiyotiwa Chachu, na siku tano baadaye tukaungana nao Troa. Tukakaa huko siku saba.
sw.R: Sisi tulisafiri kwa meli kutoka Filipi baada ya Sikukuu ya Kiyahudi ya Mikate Isiyotiwa Chachu. Siku tano baadaye tukakutana na wenzetu huko Troa. Tukakaa huko kwa juma moja.

decisions.choice: the days of Unleavened Bread: the seven-day festival that followed Passover
decisions.reason: Exodus 12:15-20 and Luke 22:1. Luke dates the journey by the Jewish calendar; Pentecost (20:16) came seven weeks after Passover.

decisions.choice: within five days: the crossing took five days
alternatives: they arrived on the fifth day of the festival
decisions.reason: The same crossing the other way took two days (16:11); this one was slower.

decisions.choice: the Jewish Festival of Unleavened Bread
decisions.reason: Readable says what kind of days these were.

decisions.choice: a week
decisions.reason: Plainer English for the same length of time.

decisions.choice: los Ázimos (L); la fiesta de los Panes sin Levadura (B, R)
decisions.reason: The term-sheet rendering: Literal keeps the Greek's one word, the old Spanish name of the feast; Balanced and Readable name the feast in words every reader knows (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: les Pains sans levain, with a capital
decisions.reason: The name of the festival (m1), capitalised as a feast's name; "les azymes" is a technical word few readers know.

source.text: Ἐν δὲ τῇ μιᾷ τῶν σαββάτων συνηγμένων ἡμῶν κλάσαι ἄρτον ὁ Παῦλος διελέγετο αὐτοῖς, μέλλων ἐξιέναι τῇ ἐπαύριον, παρέτεινέν τε τὸν λόγον μέχρι μεσονυκτίου.

records.literal_gloss: On then the first of the week, having been gathered together we to break bread, the Paul was discussing with them, being about to depart on the next day, he prolonged and the word until midnight.

en.L: And on the first [day] of the week, when we had gathered to break bread, Paul was talking with them, since he was about to depart the next day, and he prolonged [his] message until midnight.
en.B: On the first day of the week we met together to break bread. Paul spoke with the people there, because he intended to leave the next day, and his talk went on until midnight.
en.R: On the first day of the week, we met together to break bread and share the Lord's meal. Paul was planning to leave the next day, so he talked with the believers for a long time. He kept talking until midnight.

es.L: Y el primer [día] de la semana, reunidos nosotros para partir pan, Pablo conversaba con ellos, pues iba a salir al día siguiente, y prolongó [su] discurso hasta la medianoche.
es.B: El primer día de la semana nos reunimos para partir el pan. Pablo habló con los que estaban allí, porque tenía intención de irse al día siguiente, y su charla se alargó hasta la medianoche.
es.R: El primer día de la semana nos reunimos para partir el pan y compartir la Cena del Señor. Pablo pensaba irse al día siguiente, así que habló largo rato con los creyentes. Siguió hablando hasta la medianoche.

fr.L: Et le premier [jour] de la semaine, alors que nous étions réunis pour rompre le pain, Paul s’entretenait avec eux, devant partir le lendemain, et il prolongea [son] discours jusqu’à minuit.
fr.B: Le premier jour de la semaine, nous nous réunîmes pour rompre le pain. Paul s’entretint avec ceux qui étaient là, parce qu’il voulait partir le lendemain, et son discours se prolongea jusqu’à minuit.
fr.R: Le premier jour de la semaine, nous nous sommes réunis pour rompre le pain et partager le repas du Seigneur. Paul avait l’intention de partir le lendemain. Alors il a parlé longtemps avec les croyants. Il a continué à parler jusqu’à minuit.

sw.L: Na siku ya kwanza ya juma, tulipokuwa tumekusanyika kumega mkate, Paulo alikuwa akizungumza nao, kwa kuwa alikuwa karibu kuondoka kesho yake, naye akaendeleza [ujumbe wake] mpaka usiku wa manane.
sw.B: Siku ya kwanza ya juma tulikusanyika kumega mkate. Paulo alizungumza na watu waliokuwepo, kwa sababu alikusudia kuondoka kesho yake, na mazungumzo yake yakaendelea mpaka usiku wa manane.
sw.R: Siku ya kwanza ya juma tulikutana pamoja kumega mkate na kushiriki Chakula cha Bwana. Paulo alikuwa amepanga kuondoka kesho yake, kwa hiyo alizungumza na waumini kwa muda mrefu. Aliendelea kuzungumza mpaka usiku wa manane.

decisions.choice: the first day of the week: the day after the Sabbath, the day Jesus rose
decisions.reason: Luke 24:1 uses the same phrase. If the day was counted from sunset, as Jews counted it, the meeting was on what is now Saturday evening; if from midnight or dawn, on Sunday evening. The text does not settle it. See also 1 Corinthians 16:2.

decisions.choice: to break bread: a shared meal that included the Lord's Supper
decisions.reason: "Breaking bread" is used of the believers' meals together (2:42, 2:46) and of Jesus's meals (Luke 22:19, 24:30, 24:35). Paul calls the cup and the bread a sharing in Christ (1 Corinthians 10:16; 11:20-26). Here the gathering is for this purpose.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "we" had gathered
alternatives: many later manuscripts read "the disciples" had gathered
decisions.reason: The early manuscripts keep the first person here. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: was talking: speaking and discussing
decisions.reason: The verb is used of reasoning and discussion (17:2, 18:4, 19:8). In 20:11 a plainer word for conversation is used.

decisions.choice: share the Lord's meal; the believers
decisions.reason: Readable explains breaking bread, following the meaning note, and says who "them" are.

source.text: ἦσαν δὲ λαμπάδες ἱκαναὶ ἐν τῷ ὑπερῴῳ οὗ ἦμεν συνηγμένοι·

records.literal_gloss: There were then lamps many in the upper room where we were gathered.

en.L: Now there were many lamps in the upper room where we were gathered.
en.B: There were plenty of lamps in the upstairs room where we had gathered.
en.R: Many oil lamps were burning in the upstairs room where we were meeting.

es.L: Y había muchas lámparas en el aposento alto donde estábamos reunidos.
es.B: Había bastantes lámparas en la sala del piso de arriba donde nos habíamos reunido.
es.R: En la sala del piso de arriba donde nos reuníamos ardían muchas lámparas de aceite.

fr.L: Or il y avait beaucoup de lampes dans la chambre haute où nous étions réunis.
fr.B: Il y avait bon nombre de lampes dans la pièce de l’étage où nous étions réunis.
fr.R: Beaucoup de lampes à huile brûlaient dans la pièce à l’étage où nous nous réunissions.

sw.L: Na kulikuwa na taa nyingi katika chumba cha ghorofani tulimokuwa tumekusanyika.
sw.B: Kulikuwa na taa nyingi katika chumba cha ghorofani tulimokutania.
sw.R: Taa nyingi za mafuta zilikuwa zikiwaka katika chumba cha ghorofani tulimokuwa tukikutania.

decisions.choice: many lamps: oil lamps, which gave off heat and smoke
alternatives: a detail with no bearing on the story
decisions.reason: Luke may mention them to explain the warm, close air that made the young man drowsy (20:9), or simply as a witness's memory. The text does not say why.

decisions.choice: upper room: a room on an upper floor
decisions.reason: As in 1:13 and 9:37. 20:9 shows it was on the third floor.

decisions.choice: oil lamps were burning
decisions.reason: Readable says what kind of lamps they were.

source.text: καθεζόμενος δέ τις νεανίας ὀνόματι Εὔτυχος ἐπὶ τῆς θυρίδος, καταφερόμενος ὕπνῳ βαθεῖ διαλεγομένου τοῦ Παύλου ἐπὶ πλεῖον, κατενεχθεὶς ἀπὸ τοῦ ὕπνου ἔπεσεν ἀπὸ τοῦ τριστέγου κάτω καὶ ἤρθη νεκρός.

records.literal_gloss: Sitting then a certain young man by name Eutychus on the window, being overcome by sleep deep, Paul discussing for longer, having been overcome by the sleep he fell from the third story down and was taken up dead.

en.L: And a certain young man named Eutychus, sitting in the window, was being overcome by deep sleep as Paul talked still longer; overcome by sleep, he fell down from the third story and was picked up dead.
en.B: A young man named Eutychus sat in the window opening. Paul's talk ran longer and longer, and Eutychus sank into a heavy sleep. Overcome by it, he fell from the third floor to the ground, and when they lifted him up he was dead.
en.R: A young man named Eutychus was sitting in an open window. Paul talked for a very long time, and Eutychus got sleepier and sleepier. At last he fell fast asleep and fell out of the window. He fell from the third floor all the way to the ground. When the people picked him up, he was dead.

es.L: Y un joven llamado Eutico, sentado en la ventana, iba siendo vencido por un sueño profundo mientras Pablo seguía hablando más y más; vencido por el sueño, cayó desde el tercer piso abajo y fue levantado muerto.
es.B: Un joven llamado Eutico estaba sentado en el hueco de la ventana. Como la charla de Pablo se alargaba cada vez más, Eutico se fue hundiendo en un sueño profundo. Vencido por el sueño, cayó desde el tercer piso hasta el suelo, y cuando lo levantaron estaba muerto.
es.R: Un joven llamado Eutico estaba sentado en una ventana abierta. Pablo habló durante mucho tiempo, y a Eutico le daba cada vez más sueño. Al final se quedó profundamente dormido y se cayó por la ventana. Cayó desde el tercer piso hasta el suelo. Cuando la gente lo levantó, estaba muerto.

fr.L: Et un jeune homme nommé Eutyque, assis à la fenêtre, était gagné par un profond sommeil pendant que Paul discourait plus longtemps ; vaincu par le sommeil, il tomba du troisième niveau en bas et fut relevé mort.
fr.B: Un jeune homme nommé Eutyque était assis dans l’embrasure de la fenêtre. Comme Paul prolongeait son discours, Eutyque s’enfonça dans un profond sommeil. Vaincu par le sommeil, il tomba du deuxième étage jusqu’en bas, et quand on le releva, il était mort.
fr.R: Un jeune homme appelé Eutyque était assis au bord d’une fenêtre ouverte. Paul a parlé très longtemps, et Eutyque avait de plus en plus sommeil. Finalement, il s’est profondément endormi, et il est tombé par la fenêtre. Il est tombé du deuxième étage jusque sur le sol. Quand les gens l’ont relevé, il était mort.

sw.L: Na kijana mmoja kwa jina Eutiko, akiwa ameketi dirishani, alikuwa akilemewa na usingizi mzito Paulo alipokuwa akizungumza kwa muda mrefu zaidi; akiwa amelemewa na usingizi, alianguka chini kutoka ghorofa ya tatu, akainuliwa akiwa amekufa.
sw.B: Kijana mmoja aitwaye Eutiko alikuwa ameketi dirishani. Paulo alipoendelea kuzungumza kwa muda mrefu zaidi na zaidi, Eutiko alizama katika usingizi mzito. Usingizi ulipomshinda, alianguka kutoka ghorofa ya tatu hadi chini, na walipomwinua alikuwa amekufa.
sw.R: Kijana mmoja aitwaye Eutiko alikuwa ameketi katika dirisha lililokuwa wazi. Paulo alizungumza kwa muda mrefu sana, na Eutiko akazidi kusinzia. Mwishowe alipitiwa na usingizi mzito, akaanguka kutoka dirishani. Alianguka kutoka ghorofa ya tatu mpaka chini kabisa. Watu walipomwokota, alikuwa amekufa.

decisions.choice: the window: an opening in the wall, with no glass
decisions.reason: Windows were open spaces, sometimes with shutters, wide enough to sit in.

decisions.choice: two steps: he was sinking into sleep, then sleep overcame him
decisions.reason: The first participle is present, of a process; the second is aorist, of the moment he was overcome.

decisions.choice: was picked up dead: he had died
decisions.reason: Luke says "dead", not "as if dead"; compare 14:19, where the crowd only supposed Paul was dead. 20:10 and 20:12 tell of him alive again.

decisions.choice: fell out of the window
decisions.reason: Readable says where he fell from, which the story implies.

decisions.choice: du troisième niveau (L); du deuxième étage (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek and the English count the ground floor as the first story. French counts floors above the ground floor ("rez-de-chaussée"), so the third story is "le deuxième étage"; "troisième étage" would make the fall one floor higher. Literal keeps the Greek count with "niveau".

decisions.choice: ghorofa ya tatu
decisions.reason: The Greek counts the ground floor as the first story, so the room was two floors above the ground. Where Swahili counts "ghorofa" only above the ground floor, a reader may take "ghorofa ya tatu" as one floor higher than meant; a reviewer may prefer "ghorofa ya pili".

source.text: καταβὰς δὲ ὁ Παῦλος ἐπέπεσεν αὐτῷ καὶ συμπεριλαβὼν εἶπεν· Μὴ θορυβεῖσθε, ἡ γὰρ ψυχὴ αὐτοῦ ἐν αὐτῷ ἐστιν.

records.literal_gloss: Having gone down then Paul fell upon him and having embraced said, Not be alarmed, the for life of him in him is.

en.L: But Paul went down, fell upon him, and taking [him] in his arms said, "Do not be alarmed, for his life is in him."
en.B: Paul went down, threw himself on the young man, and held him close. "Do not be upset," he said, "his life is in him."
en.R: Paul went downstairs. He lay down on top of the young man and put his arms around him. Then he said to the people, "Do not be upset! He is alive."

es.L: Pero Pablo bajó, se echó sobre él y, tras abrazar[lo], dijo: «No {{plural_you:se alarmen|os alarméis}}, porque su vida está en él».
es.B: Pablo bajó, se echó sobre el joven y lo abrazó. «No {{plural_you:se angustien|os angustiéis}}», dijo, «su vida está en él».
es.R: Pablo bajó. Se tendió sobre el joven y lo rodeó con sus brazos. Luego le dijo a la gente: «¡No {{plural_you:se angustien|os angustiéis}}! Está vivo».

fr.L: Mais Paul, étant descendu, se jeta sur lui et, [le] prenant dans ses bras, dit : « Ne vous troublez pas, car sa vie est en lui. »
fr.B: Paul descendit, se jeta sur le jeune homme et le serra dans ses bras. « Ne vous inquiétez pas, dit-il, sa vie est en lui. »
fr.R: Paul est descendu. Il s’est couché sur le jeune homme et il l’a pris dans ses bras. Puis il a dit aux gens : « Ne vous inquiétez pas ! Il est vivant. »

sw.L: Lakini Paulo, akiisha kushuka, alijilaza juu yake, na akimkumbatia akasema, "Msifadhaike, kwa maana uhai wake umo ndani yake."
sw.B: Paulo alishuka, akajitupa juu ya yule kijana, akamkumbatia. Akasema, "Msifadhaike; uhai wake umo ndani yake."
sw.R: Paulo alishuka chini. Akajilaza juu ya yule kijana, akamkumbatia. Kisha akawaambia watu, "Msihuzunike! Yu hai."

decisions.choice: fell upon him and embraced him: as Elijah and Elisha did over dead boys
decisions.reason: Elijah stretched himself on the widow's son (1 Kings 17:21) and Elisha lay on the Shunammite's son (2 Kings 4:34), and both boys lived.

decisions.choice: do not be alarmed: stop the noisy distress of mourning
decisions.reason: The verb is used of the mourners' uproar in Mark 5:39. Its noun was the uproar of 20:1.

decisions.choice: his life is in him: he is alive now
decisions.reason: 20:9 says he was picked up dead and 20:12 that they brought him away alive. Paul's words announce that his life has returned, as Peter's do in 9:40.

decisions.choice: He is alive.
decisions.reason: Readable gives the plain sense of the phrase.

decisions.choice: ustedes / vosotros forms
decisions.reason: Every plural "you" in this chapter, here and in Paul's speech to the elders (20:18-35), and its verb, is the plural_you setting: ustedes (Latin America, the default) or vosotros (Spain).

source.text: ἀναβὰς δὲ καὶ κλάσας τὸν ἄρτον καὶ γευσάμενος ἐφ’ ἱκανόν τε ὁμιλήσας ἄχρι αὐγῆς, οὕτως ἐξῆλθεν.

records.literal_gloss: Having gone up then and having broken the bread and having eaten, for long and having talked until daybreak, thus he departed.

en.L: And having gone up and broken the bread and eaten, and having talked a long while, until daybreak, so he departed.
en.B: Then he went back upstairs, broke the bread and ate. He went on talking with them a long time, until dawn, and then he left.
en.R: Then Paul went back upstairs. He broke the bread and ate with them. He kept talking with them until the sun came up. Then he left.

es.L: Y habiendo subido, y partido el pan y comido, y habiendo conversado largo rato hasta el alba, así se fue.
es.B: Luego volvió a subir, partió el pan y comió. Siguió conversando con ellos largo rato, hasta el amanecer, y después se marchó.
es.R: Después Pablo volvió a subir. Partió el pan y comió con ellos. Siguió hablando con ellos hasta que salió el sol. Entonces se fue.

fr.L: Et étant remonté, ayant rompu le pain et ayant mangé, et ayant parlé longtemps, jusqu’à l’aube, ainsi il partit.
fr.B: Puis il remonta, rompit le pain et mangea. Il continua de s’entretenir longtemps avec eux, jusqu’à l’aube, et ensuite il partit.
fr.R: Ensuite Paul est remonté. Il a rompu le pain et il a mangé avec eux. Il a continué à leur parler jusqu’au lever du soleil. Puis il est parti.

sw.L: Na akiisha kupanda juu na kumega mkate na kula, na kuzungumza nao kwa muda mrefu mpaka mapambazuko, hivyo akaondoka.
sw.B: Kisha akarudi ghorofani, akamega mkate, akala. Akaendelea kuzungumza nao kwa muda mrefu mpaka alfajiri, kisha akaondoka.
sw.R: Kisha Paulo akarudi juu ghorofani. Akamega mkate, akala pamoja nao. Akaendelea kuzungumza nao mpaka jua lilipochomoza. Kisha akaondoka.

decisions.choice: the bread: the bread they had gathered to break (20:7)
decisions.reason: The article points back to 20:7. The meal comes after midnight, once Eutychus is restored.

decisions.choice: talked: conversed
decisions.reason: The verb is used of ordinary conversation (Luke 24:14-15), unlike the discussion of 20:7 and 20:9.

decisions.choice: ate with them
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that it was a shared meal.

source.text: ἤγαγον δὲ τὸν παῖδα ζῶντα, καὶ παρεκλήθησαν οὐ μετρίως.

records.literal_gloss: They brought then the boy living, and were comforted not moderately.

en.L: And they brought the boy [away] alive, and were comforted not a little.
en.B: They led the boy away alive, and they were greatly comforted.
en.R: The people took the young man home alive. They were very glad and greatly comforted.

es.L: Y llevaron al muchacho vivo, y fueron consolados no poco.
es.B: Se llevaron al muchacho vivo, y quedaron muy consolados.
es.R: La gente llevó al joven a su casa con vida. Estaban muy contentos y muy consolados.

fr.L: Et ils amenèrent le garçon vivant, et ils furent consolés, et non médiocrement.
fr.B: On ramena le garçon vivant, et ce fut pour tous un grand réconfort.
fr.R: Les gens ont ramené le jeune homme chez lui, vivant. Ils étaient très heureux et très réconfortés.

sw.L: Na wakamleta yule kijana akiwa hai, wakafarijika si kidogo.
sw.B: Wakamchukua yule kijana akiwa hai, wakafarijika sana.
sw.R: Watu walimpeleka yule kijana nyumbani akiwa hai. Walifurahi sana na kufarijika mno.

decisions.choice: the boy: the young man of 20:9
decisions.reason: The word can mean a child, a youth or a servant. It refers to Eutychus, whom 20:9 calls a young man.

decisions.choice: not a little: very much
decisions.reason: Luke often says much by saying "not a little" (12:18, 19:23, 19:24).

decisions.choice: took home; very glad
decisions.reason: Readable supplies where they took him and what comfort meant to them here. "Home" is not in the Greek.

source.text: Ἡμεῖς δὲ προελθόντες ἐπὶ τὸ πλοῖον ἀνήχθημεν ἐπὶ τὴν Ἆσσον, ἐκεῖθεν μέλλοντες ἀναλαμβάνειν τὸν Παῦλον, οὕτως γὰρ διατεταγμένος ἦν μέλλων αὐτὸς πεζεύειν.

records.literal_gloss: We then having gone ahead to the ship set sail for Assos, from there being about to take on board the Paul; thus for having arranged he was, being about himself to go on foot.

en.L: But we, going ahead to the ship, set sail for Assos, intending to take Paul on board there, for so he had arranged, intending himself to go on foot.
en.B: We went on ahead to the ship and sailed for Assos, where we meant to take Paul on board. He had arranged it this way, because he wanted to go there on foot.
en.R: The rest of us went ahead to the ship and sailed to the town of Assos. We planned to pick Paul up there. Paul had planned it this way because he wanted to walk to Assos by land.

es.L: Pero nosotros, adelantándonos hasta el barco, zarpamos hacia Asón, con la intención de recoger allí a Pablo, porque así lo había dispuesto él, pues pensaba ir a pie.
es.B: Nosotros nos adelantamos hasta el barco y zarpamos hacia Asón, donde pensábamos recoger a Pablo. Él lo había dispuesto así, porque quería ir hasta allí a pie.
es.R: Los demás nos adelantamos hasta el barco y navegamos hasta el pueblo de Asón. Pensábamos recoger allí a Pablo. Pablo lo había planeado así porque quería ir caminando por tierra hasta Asón.

fr.L: Mais nous, ayant pris les devants vers le bateau, nous embarquâmes pour Assos, devant de là prendre Paul à bord, car il l’avait ainsi réglé, devant lui-même faire la route à pied.
fr.B: Nous, nous partîmes en avant vers le bateau et fîmes voile vers Assos, où nous devions prendre Paul à bord. Il l’avait réglé ainsi, parce qu’il voulait faire le trajet à pied.
fr.R: Nous autres, nous sommes allés en avance jusqu’au bateau, et nous avons navigué jusqu’à la ville d’Assos. Nous avions prévu de prendre Paul là-bas. Paul avait organisé les choses ainsi parce qu’il voulait aller à Assos à pied, par la terre.

sw.L: Lakini sisi, tukiisha kutangulia kwenye meli, tuling'oa nanga kwenda Aso, tukikusudia kumpakia Paulo huko; kwa maana ndivyo alivyokuwa ameagiza, akikusudia yeye mwenyewe kwenda kwa miguu.
sw.B: Sisi tulitangulia kwenye meli, tukasafiri kwenda Aso, ambako tulikusudia kumpakia Paulo. Alikuwa amepanga hivyo, kwa sababu alitaka kwenda huko kwa miguu.
sw.R: Sisi wengine tulitangulia kwenye meli, tukasafiri mpaka mji wa Aso. Tulipanga kumchukua Paulo huko. Paulo alikuwa amepanga hivyo, kwa sababu alitaka kutembea kwa miguu mpaka Aso kwa njia ya nchi kavu.

decisions.choice: Assos: a port south of Troas
decisions.reason: By road Assos was about twenty miles from Troas; by sea the ship had to round a cape.

decisions.choice: he himself was to go on foot: Paul alone went overland
decisions.reason: "Himself" sets Paul apart from the "we" who sailed. Luke does not give his reason.

decisions.choice: the rest of us; by land
decisions.reason: Readable makes the two routes clear.

decisions.choice: meli
decisions.reason: "meli", the everyday word for a sea-going ship, as in Acts 28; used for every ship in this journey.

source.text: ὡς δὲ συνέβαλλεν ἡμῖν εἰς τὴν Ἆσσον, ἀναλαβόντες αὐτὸν ἤλθομεν εἰς Μιτυλήνην, κἀκεῖθεν ἀποπλεύσαντες τῇ ἐπιούσῃ κατηντήσαμεν ἄντικρυς Χίου, τῇ δὲ ἑτέρᾳ παρεβάλομεν εἰς Σάμον, τῇ δὲ ἐχομένῃ ἤλθομεν εἰς Μίλητον·

records.literal_gloss: When then he met with us at the Assos, having taken up him we came to Mitylene, \v 15 and from there having sailed away on the following [day] we arrived opposite Chios, then on the other [day] we crossed over to Samos, and on the next [day] we came to Miletus.

en.L: And when he met us at Assos, having taken him on board we came to Mitylene; \v 15 and sailing from there, on the following [day] we arrived opposite Chios, and on the next [day] we crossed over to Samos, and on the [day] after we came to Miletus.
en.B: When he met us at Assos, we took him aboard and went on to Mitylene. \v 15 We sailed from there and the next day arrived off Chios. The day after that we crossed to Samos, and a day later we reached Miletus.
en.R: Paul met us at Assos, and we took him on board. Then we sailed to Mitylene. \v 15 The next day we sailed from there and came to a place across the water from the island of Chios. The day after that we crossed over to the island of Samos. One day later we arrived at the city of Miletus.

es.L: Y cuando nos alcanzó en Asón, tomándolo a bordo, llegamos a Mitilene; \v 15 y zarpando de allí, al [día] siguiente llegamos frente a Quío, y al otro [día] cruzamos a Samos, y al [día] siguiente llegamos a Mileto.
es.B: Cuando se reunió con nosotros en Asón, lo tomamos a bordo y seguimos hasta Mitilene. \v 15 Zarpamos de allí y al día siguiente llegamos frente a Quío. Al otro día cruzamos a Samos, y un día después llegamos a Mileto.
es.R: Pablo se encontró con nosotros en Asón, y lo subimos al barco. Luego navegamos hasta Mitilene. \v 15 Al día siguiente salimos de allí y llegamos a un lugar frente a la isla de Quío. Al otro día cruzamos hasta la isla de Samos. Un día después llegamos a la ciudad de Mileto.

fr.L: Et quand il nous rejoignit à Assos, l’ayant pris à bord, nous vînmes à Mitylène ; \v 15 et de là, ayant fait voile, le [jour] suivant nous arrivâmes en face de Chios, et le [jour] d’après nous passâmes à Samos, et le [jour] qui suivit nous vînmes à Milet.
fr.B: Quand il nous eut rejoints à Assos, nous le prîmes à bord et nous gagnâmes Mitylène. \v 15 De là, nous reprîmes la mer, et le lendemain nous arrivâmes à la hauteur de Chios. Le jour suivant, nous fîmes la traversée jusqu’à Samos, et le jour d’après, nous atteignîmes Milet.
fr.R: Paul nous a retrouvés à Assos, et nous l’avons pris à bord. Ensuite, nous sommes allés en bateau jusqu’à Mitylène. \v 15 Le lendemain, nous sommes repartis de là, et nous sommes arrivés en face de l’île de Chios. Le jour suivant, nous avons traversé jusqu’à l’île de Samos. Un jour plus tard, nous sommes arrivés dans la ville de Milet.

sw.L: Na alipokutana nasi huko Aso, tukiisha kumpakia, tulifika Mitilene; \v 15 na kutoka huko tukiisha kusafiri, [siku] iliyofuata tulifika mkabala wa Kio, na [siku] nyingine tukavuka hadi Samo, na [siku] iliyofuata tukafika Mileto.
sw.B: Alipokutana nasi Aso, tukampakia melini, tukaendelea mpaka Mitilene. \v 15 Tukasafiri kutoka huko, na kesho yake tukafika karibu na Kio. Siku iliyofuata tukavuka mpaka Samo, na siku moja baadaye tukafika Mileto.
sw.R: Paulo alikutana nasi Aso, nasi tukampakia melini. Kisha tukasafiri mpaka Mitilene. \v 15 Kesho yake tuliondoka huko, tukafika mahali palipokuwa ng'ambo ya kisiwa cha Kio. Siku iliyofuata tukavuka mpaka kisiwa cha Samo. Siku moja baadaye tukafika katika mji wa Mileto.

decisions.choice: the places: Mitylene on the island of Lesbos, the islands of Chios and Samos, and the port of Miletus
decisions.reason: The ship worked its way south along the coast of Asia, stopping each night. Miletus lay about thirty miles south of Ephesus.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "to Samos, and on the next day"
alternatives: many manuscripts add "and having stayed at Trogyllium" after Samos
decisions.reason: Trogyllium is a point on the mainland across from Samos. The words are in many later manuscripts and in Codex Bezae, but not in the early manuscripts the SBLGNT follows. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: opposite Chios: off the island, across the strait
decisions.reason: The word means facing; they anchored off the island, not at its harbor.

decisions.choice: the island of; the city of
decisions.reason: Readable says what each place is.

source.text: κεκρίκει γὰρ ὁ Παῦλος παραπλεῦσαι τὴν Ἔφεσον, ὅπως μὴ γένηται αὐτῷ χρονοτριβῆσαι ἐν τῇ Ἀσίᾳ, ἔσπευδεν γὰρ εἰ δυνατὸν εἴη αὐτῷ τὴν ἡμέραν τῆς πεντηκοστῆς γενέσθαι εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα.

records.literal_gloss: Had decided for the Paul to sail past the Ephesus, so that not it might happen to him to spend time in the Asia; he was hurrying for, if possible it might be for him, the day of the Pentecost to be in Jerusalem.

en.L: For Paul had decided to sail past Ephesus, so that he might not have to spend time in Asia; for he was hurrying, if it were possible for him, to be in Jerusalem [on] the day of Pentecost.
en.B: Paul had decided to sail on past Ephesus so as not to lose time in the province of Asia. He was in a hurry to reach Jerusalem, if he could, by the day of Pentecost.
en.R: Paul did not want to stop in Ephesus, because then he would have to spend too much time in the province of Asia. So he had decided to sail on past it. He was hurrying because he wanted to be in Jerusalem for the Festival of Pentecost, if he could.

es.L: Porque Pablo había decidido pasar de largo Éfeso, para que no le ocurriera perder tiempo en Asia, pues se apresuraba, si le era posible, a estar en Jerusalén el día de Pentecostés.
es.B: Pablo había decidido pasar de largo por Éfeso para no perder tiempo en la provincia de Asia. Tenía prisa por llegar a Jerusalén, si podía, para el día de Pentecostés.
es.R: Pablo no quería detenerse en Éfeso, porque entonces tendría que pasar demasiado tiempo en la provincia de Asia. Por eso había decidido seguir navegando sin parar allí. Se daba prisa porque quería estar en Jerusalén para la fiesta de Pentecostés, si era posible.

fr.L: Car Paul avait décidé de passer au large d’Éphèse, afin de ne pas avoir à s’attarder en Asie ; car il se hâtait, si cela lui était possible, d’être à Jérusalem le jour de la Pentecôte.
fr.B: Paul avait décidé de passer au large d’Éphèse sans s’y arrêter, pour ne pas perdre de temps dans la province d’Asie. Il avait hâte d’arriver à Jérusalem, si possible, pour le jour de la Pentecôte.
fr.R: Paul ne voulait pas s’arrêter à Éphèse, parce qu’alors il aurait dû passer trop de temps dans la province d’Asie. Il avait donc décidé de passer devant Éphèse sans s’arrêter. Il se dépêchait, parce qu’il voulait être à Jérusalem pour la fête de la Pentecôte, s’il le pouvait.

sw.L: Kwa maana Paulo alikuwa ameamua kupita Efeso kwa meli bila kusimama, ili asipoteze muda katika Asia; kwa maana alikuwa akiharakisha, kama ingewezekana kwake, kuwa Yerusalemu siku ya Pentekoste.
sw.B: Paulo alikuwa ameamua kupita Efeso bila kusimama, ili asipoteze muda katika jimbo la Asia. Alikuwa na haraka kufika Yerusalemu, kama ingewezekana, kufikia siku ya Pentekoste.
sw.R: Paulo hakutaka kusimama Efeso, kwa sababu angelazimika kukaa muda mrefu mno katika jimbo la Asia. Kwa hiyo alikuwa ameamua kupita bila kusimama. Alikuwa na haraka kwa sababu alitaka kuwa Yerusalemu wakati wa Sikukuu ya Pentekoste, kama ingewezekana.

decisions.choice: the day of Pentecost: the Festival of Weeks, fifty days after Passover
decisions.reason: Leviticus 23:15-21; Acts 2:1. Paul left Philippi after the days of Unleavened Bread (20:6), so he had less than seven weeks to reach Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: Asia: the Roman province whose chief city was Ephesus
decisions.reason: As in 16:6 and 19:10.

decisions.choice: sail past Ephesus: not call there, to save time
decisions.reason: Luke gives the reason himself: Paul was in a hurry. A visit would have kept him there.

decisions.choice: the Festival of Pentecost
decisions.reason: Readable says that Pentecost was a festival.

source.text: Ἀπὸ δὲ τῆς Μιλήτου πέμψας εἰς Ἔφεσον μετεκαλέσατο τοὺς πρεσβυτέρους τῆς ἐκκλησίας.

records.literal_gloss: From then the Miletus having sent to Ephesus he summoned the elders of the church.

en.L: And from Miletus, sending to Ephesus, he summoned the elders of the church.
en.B: From Miletus he sent word to Ephesus and called the elders of the church to come to him.
en.R: While Paul was at Miletus, he sent a message to Ephesus. He asked the leaders of the church there, the elders, to come and meet him.

es.L: Y desde Mileto, enviando [aviso] a Éfeso, hizo llamar a los ancianos de la iglesia.
es.B: Desde Mileto mandó aviso a Éfeso para que los ancianos de la iglesia vinieran a verlo.
es.R: Mientras Pablo estaba en Mileto, envió un mensaje a Éfeso. Pidió a los líderes de la iglesia de allí, los ancianos, que vinieran a reunirse con él.

fr.L: Et de Milet, ayant envoyé [quelqu’un] à Éphèse, il fit appeler les anciens de l’église.
fr.B: De Milet, il envoya un message à Éphèse pour faire venir auprès de lui les anciens de l’église.
fr.R: Pendant que Paul était à Milet, il a envoyé un message à Éphèse. Il a demandé aux dirigeants de l’église de là-bas, les anciens, de venir le voir.

sw.L: Na kutoka Mileto, akituma [ujumbe] Efeso, aliwaita wazee wa kanisa.
sw.B: Kutoka Mileto alituma ujumbe Efeso, akawaita wazee wa kanisa waje kwake.
sw.R: Paulo alipokuwa Mileto, alituma ujumbe Efeso. Aliwaomba viongozi wa kanisa la huko, yaani wazee, waje kukutana naye.

decisions.choice: elders: the leaders of a local church
decisions.reason: Paul and Barnabas appointed elders in each church (14:23); the Jerusalem church had them too (11:30, 15:2). In 20:28 Paul calls these same men overseers.

decisions.choice: from Miletus to Ephesus: a journey of some days there and back
decisions.reason: Ephesus lay about thirty miles to the north, so the message and the elders' journey took time.

decisions.choice: the leaders of the church there, the elders
decisions.reason: Readable explains what elders are, and keeps the word.

decisions.choice: ancianos (L, B); los líderes de la iglesia ..., los ancianos (R)
decisions.reason: The term-sheet rendering for the church office. Readable says "líderes de la iglesia" and keeps "ancianos" beside it, as the English Readable does (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: les anciens de l’église, with a lowercase "église"
decisions.reason: As the term sheet settles: "les anciens" for the elders (m1), and "l’église" in lowercase for one congregation, here the believers of Ephesus. In 20:28 "l’Église de Dieu" takes the capital, as God's whole people.

source.text: ὡς δὲ παρεγένοντο πρὸς αὐτὸν εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ὑμεῖς ἐπίστασθε ἀπὸ πρώτης ἡμέρας ἀφ’ ἧς ἐπέβην εἰς τὴν Ἀσίαν πῶς μεθ’ ὑμῶν τὸν πάντα χρόνον ἐγενόμην, δουλεύων τῷ κυρίῳ μετὰ πάσης ταπεινοφροσύνης καὶ δακρύων καὶ πειρασμῶν τῶν συμβάντων μοι ἐν ταῖς ἐπιβουλαῖς τῶν Ἰουδαίων·

records.literal_gloss: When then they came to him he said to them, You know, from [the] first day from which I set foot in the Asia, how with you the whole time I was, \v 19 serving the Lord with all humility and tears and trials the having happened to me by the plots of the Jews,

en.L: And when they had come to him, he said to them, "You know how I was with you the whole time from the first day that I set foot in Asia, \v 19 serving the Lord as a slave with all humility and tears and trials that came upon me through the plots of the Jews;
en.B: When they had come, he said to them, "From the first day I set foot in the province of Asia, you have seen what kind of life I led among you the whole time. \v 19 I worked as the Lord's servant, with all humility and with tears, enduring the trials that the plots of the Jews brought on me.
en.R: When they came, Paul said to them, "You know what my life was like all the time I was with you, from the very first day I came to the province of Asia. \v 19 I served the Lord as {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servant. I was humble, and I often cried. I had many troubles because some of the Jews made plans against me.

es.L: Y cuando llegaron a él, les dijo: «{{plural_you:Ustedes saben|Vosotros sabéis}}, desde el primer día en que puse pie en Asia, cómo estuve con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} todo el tiempo, \v 19 sirviendo como esclavo al Señor con toda humildad y lágrimas y pruebas que me sobrevinieron por las conspiraciones de los judíos;
es.B: Cuando llegaron, les dijo: «Desde el primer día que puse pie en la provincia de Asia, {{plural_you:han visto|habéis visto}} cómo viví entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} todo el tiempo. \v 19 Serví al Señor como siervo suyo, con toda humildad y con lágrimas, soportando las pruebas que me trajeron las conspiraciones de los judíos.
es.R: Cuando llegaron, Pablo les dijo: «{{plural_you:Ustedes saben|Vosotros sabéis}} cómo fue mi vida todo el tiempo que estuve con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, desde el primer día que llegué a la provincia de Asia. \v 19 Serví al Señor como {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} siervo. Fui humilde, y muchas veces lloré. Tuve muchos problemas porque algunos judíos hicieron planes contra mí.

fr.L: Et quand ils furent arrivés auprès de lui, il leur dit : « Vous savez, depuis le premier jour où j’ai mis le pied en Asie, comment j’ai été avec vous tout le temps, \v 19 servant le Seigneur comme esclave, en toute humilité, avec larmes et épreuves qui me sont arrivées par les complots des Juifs ;
fr.B: Quand ils furent arrivés, il leur dit : « Depuis le premier jour où j’ai mis le pied dans la province d’Asie, vous avez vu quelle vie j’ai menée parmi vous tout ce temps. \v 19 J’ai travaillé comme serviteur du Seigneur, en toute humilité et avec des larmes, au milieu des épreuves que m’ont attirées les complots des Juifs.
fr.R: Quand ils sont arrivés, Paul leur a dit : « Vous savez comment j’ai vécu pendant tout le temps que j’ai passé avec vous, depuis le tout premier jour où je suis arrivé dans la province d’Asie. \v 19 J’ai servi le Seigneur comme {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} serviteur. J’ai été humble, et j’ai souvent pleuré. J’ai eu beaucoup de difficultés parce que des Juifs ont fait des plans contre moi.

sw.L: Na walipofika kwake, aliwaambia, "Ninyi mnajua jinsi nilivyokuwa pamoja nanyi muda wote tangu siku ya kwanza nilipokanyaga Asia, \v 19 nikimtumikia Bwana kama mtumwa kwa unyenyekevu wote na machozi na majaribu yaliyonipata kwa njama za Wayahudi;
sw.B: Walipofika, aliwaambia, "Tangu siku ya kwanza nilipokanyaga jimbo la Asia, mmeona jinsi nilivyoishi kati yenu muda wote. \v 19 Nilifanya kazi kama mtumishi wa Bwana kwa unyenyekevu wote na kwa machozi, nikivumilia majaribu yaliyonipata kwa sababu ya njama za Wayahudi.
sw.R: Walipofika, Paulo aliwaambia, "Mnajua maisha yangu yalivyokuwa wakati wote nilipokuwa pamoja nanyi, tangu siku ya kwanza nilipokuja katika jimbo la Asia. \v 19 Nilimtumikia Bwana kama mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}. Nilikuwa mnyenyekevu, na mara nyingi nililia. Nilipata taabu nyingi kwa sababu baadhi ya Wayahudi walipanga njama dhidi yangu.

decisions.choice: how I was with you: the way I lived among you
decisions.reason: Paul appeals to what they saw of his conduct, as in 1 Thessalonians 2:1-12.

decisions.choice: serving: the work of a slave for his master
decisions.reason: The verb is formed from the word for slave. Paul calls himself a slave of Christ (Romans 1:1; Philippians 1:1).

decisions.choice: trials: hardships that tested him
decisions.reason: The word can mean either; here the trials come from the plots of others.

decisions.choice: the plots of the Jews: schemes against him by some of the Jews
decisions.reason: Acts 19:9 tells of opposition in the synagogue at Ephesus, and 20:3 of a plot in Greece; the plots at Ephesus are not described.

decisions.choice: worked as the Lord's servant / served the Lord as his servant
decisions.reason: The wording keeps the idea of serving as a slave that is in the verb. "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m2) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

decisions.choice: I often cried; some of the Jews
decisions.reason: Readable says what the tears mean and that the plotters were some Jews, not all.

decisions.choice: sirviendo como esclavo (L); serví ... como siervo (B, R)
decisions.reason: The term-sheet rendering for the slave's service: Literal says "esclavo", as the English Literal says "slave" (meaning decision m2); Balanced and Readable use "siervo".

decisions.choice: comme esclave (L); serviteur (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the term sheet settles for the slave words: Literal keeps "esclave", which the verb contains (m2); Balanced and Readable say "serviteur", as the English does.

decisions.choice: kama mtumwa (L); kama mtumishi (B, R)
decisions.reason: The verb is the work of a slave for his master (meaning decision on serving); Literal keeps "mtumwa" and Balanced and Readable say "mtumishi", as the project does for doulos.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}
decisions.reason: In Swahili the deity_pronoun setting goes only on free pronouns and possessives, since pronouns marked inside the verb cannot take a capital; so this chapter has fewer spans than the English.

source.text: ὡς οὐδὲν ὑπεστειλάμην τῶν συμφερόντων τοῦ μὴ ἀναγγεῖλαι ὑμῖν καὶ διδάξαι ὑμᾶς δημοσίᾳ καὶ κατ’ οἴκους, διαμαρτυρόμενος Ἰουδαίοις τε καὶ Ἕλλησιν τὴν εἰς θεὸν μετάνοιαν καὶ πίστιν εἰς τὸν κύριον ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦν.

records.literal_gloss: how nothing I held back of the profitable things of the not to declare to you and to teach you publicly and from house to house, \v 21 testifying solemnly both to Jews and to Greeks the toward God repentance and faith in the Lord of us Jesus.

en.L: how I held back nothing of what was profitable, so as not to declare [it] to you and teach you publicly and from house to house, \v 21 solemnly testifying both to Jews and to Greeks of repentance toward God and faith in our Lord Jesus.
en.B: You know how I held back nothing that was for your good, but made it known to you and taught you, in public and from house to house. \v 21 To Jews and Greeks alike I bore solemn witness about repentance toward God and faith in our Lord Jesus.
en.R: You know that I told you everything that would help you. I did not hold anything back. I taught you in public places and in your homes. \v 21 I strongly urged both Jews and Greeks to turn away from their sins and come back to God, and to have faith in our Lord Jesus.

es.L: cómo no me guardé nada de lo que era provechoso, sin dejar de {{plural_you:anunciárselo|anunciároslo}} y de {{plural_you:enseñarles|enseñaros}} en público y de casa en casa, \v 21 dando testimonio solemne tanto a judíos como a griegos del arrepentimiento hacia Dios y de la fe en nuestro Señor Jesús.
es.B: {{plural_you:Saben|Sabéis}} que no me guardé nada de lo que {{plural_you:les|os}} convenía, sino que {{plural_you:se lo|os lo}} di a conocer y {{plural_you:les|os}} enseñé en público y de casa en casa. \v 21 A judíos y a griegos por igual les di testimonio solemne del arrepentimiento ante Dios y de la fe en nuestro Señor Jesús.
es.R: {{plural_you:Saben|Sabéis}} que {{plural_you:les|os}} dije todo lo que {{plural_you:les|os}} ayudaría. No me guardé nada. {{plural_you:Les|Os}} enseñé en lugares públicos y en {{plural_you:sus casas|vuestras casas}}. \v 21 Insistí con fuerza, tanto a judíos como a griegos, en que dejaran sus pecados y se volvieran a Dios, y en que tuvieran fe en nuestro Señor Jesús.

fr.L: comment je n’ai rien retenu de ce qui était utile, en omettant de vous l’annoncer et de vous enseigner, en public et de maison en maison, \v 21 rendant témoignage avec insistance, aux Juifs comme aux Grecs, de la repentance envers Dieu et de la foi en notre Seigneur Jésus.
fr.B: Vous savez que je n’ai rien caché de ce qui était bon pour vous, mais que je vous l’ai fait connaître et que je vous ai instruits, en public et de maison en maison. \v 21 Aux Juifs comme aux Grecs, j’ai rendu un témoignage solennel au sujet de la repentance envers Dieu et de la foi en notre Seigneur Jésus.
fr.R: Vous savez que je vous ai dit tout ce qui pouvait vous aider. Je n’ai rien gardé pour moi. Je vous ai instruits dans les lieux publics et dans vos maisons. \v 21 J’ai insisté auprès des Juifs et des Grecs pour qu’ils abandonnent leurs péchés et reviennent vers Dieu, et pour qu’ils aient foi en notre Seigneur Jésus.

sw.L: jinsi ambavyo sikuzuia kitu chochote kilichokuwa na faida, hata nisiwatangazie na kuwafundisha hadharani na nyumba kwa nyumba, \v 21 nikiwashuhudia kwa dhati Wayahudi na pia Wagiriki toba kwa Mungu na imani katika Bwana wetu Yesu.
sw.B: Mnajua jinsi ambavyo sikuficha kitu chochote kilichokuwa kwa faida yenu, bali niliwatangazia na kuwafundisha hadharani na nyumba kwa nyumba. \v 21 Niliwashuhudia kwa dhati Wayahudi na Wagiriki vilevile kuhusu toba ya kumrudia Mungu na imani katika Bwana wetu Yesu.
sw.R: Mnajua kwamba niliwaambia kila kitu ambacho kingewasaidia. Sikuficha chochote. Niliwafundisha mahali pa hadhara na majumbani mwenu. \v 21 Niliwasihi sana Wayahudi na Wagiriki pia waziache dhambi zao na kumrudia Mungu, na wawe na imani katika Bwana wetu Yesu.

decisions.choice: how: still depends on "you know" in 20:18
decisions.reason: The long sentence of 20:18-21 hangs on "you know".

decisions.choice: held back: shrank from, kept quiet out of fear
decisions.reason: The verb means to draw back or shrink. Paul uses it again in 20:27.

decisions.choice: Greeks: non-Jews, Gentiles
decisions.reason: In Acts "Jews and Greeks" means everyone (14:1, 18:4, 19:10).

decisions.choice: repentance: a change of mind and life, turning to God
decisions.reason: As in 2:38 and 3:19, repentance means turning back to God from sin.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "our Lord Jesus"
alternatives: many manuscripts read "our Lord Jesus Christ"
decisions.reason: The shorter reading is in several early manuscripts; many others add "Christ". Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: You know how / You know that
decisions.reason: The English starts a new sentence after 20:19, so it repeats "you know" from 20:18.

decisions.choice: turn away from their sins and come back to God
decisions.reason: Readable explains repentance, following the meaning note.

decisions.choice: je n’ai rien retenu ... en omettant de vous l’annoncer
alternatives: je n’ai rien retenu ... pour ne pas vous l’annoncer
decisions.reason: The Greek says that he held nothing back by failing to declare it; "pour ne pas" would make the silence his purpose. "En omettant de" keeps the Literal order and the sense (m2).

source.text: καὶ νῦν ἰδοὺ δεδεμένος ἐγὼ τῷ πνεύματι πορεύομαι εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ, τὰ ἐν αὐτῇ συναντήσοντά μοι μὴ εἰδώς, πλὴν ὅτι τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον κατὰ πόλιν διαμαρτύρεταί μοι λέγον ὅτι δεσμὰ καὶ θλίψεις με μένουσιν·

records.literal_gloss: And now behold bound I in the spirit go to Jerusalem, the things in it going to meet me not knowing, \v 23 except that the Spirit the Holy in every city testifies solemnly to me saying that chains and afflictions me await.

en.L: And now, look, bound in the Spirit, I am going to Jerusalem, not knowing the things that will meet me there, \v 23 except that the Holy Spirit solemnly testifies to me in every city, saying that chains and afflictions await me.
en.B: And now, bound by the Spirit, I am on my way to Jerusalem. What I will meet there I do not know, \v 23 except that in one city after another the Holy Spirit bears witness to me that chains and hardships lie ahead of me.
en.R: Now the Holy Spirit is leading me to Jerusalem, and I must go. I do not know what will happen to me there. \v 23 I only know this: in every city I visit, the Holy Spirit tells me that I will be put in chains and will suffer.

es.L: Y ahora, {{plural_you:miren|mirad}}, yo, atado en el Espíritu, voy a Jerusalén, sin saber lo que allí me ha de suceder, \v 23 salvo que el Espíritu Santo, ciudad por ciudad, me da testimonio solemne diciendo que me esperan cadenas y tribulaciones.
es.B: Y ahora, atado por el Espíritu, voy camino de Jerusalén. No sé lo que allí me espera, \v 23 salvo que en una ciudad tras otra el Espíritu Santo me da testimonio de que me aguardan cadenas y tribulaciones.
es.R: Ahora el Espíritu Santo me lleva a Jerusalén, y tengo que ir. No sé qué me pasará allí. \v 23 Solo sé esto: en cada ciudad que visito, el Espíritu Santo me dice que me pondrán en cadenas y que sufriré.

fr.L: Et maintenant, voici que, lié par l’Esprit, je vais à Jérusalem, ne sachant pas ce qui m’y arrivera, \v 23 sauf que l’Esprit Saint, de ville en ville, me rend témoignage en disant que des chaînes et des détresses m’attendent.
fr.B: Et maintenant, lié par l’Esprit, je me rends à Jérusalem. Ce qui m’arrivera là-bas, je l’ignore, \v 23 sauf que, de ville en ville, l’Esprit Saint m’atteste que des chaînes et des épreuves m’attendent.
fr.R: Maintenant, l’Esprit Saint me conduit à Jérusalem, et je dois y aller. Je ne sais pas ce qui m’arrivera là-bas. \v 23 Je sais seulement ceci : dans chaque ville où je passe, l’Esprit Saint me dit qu’on va me mettre des chaînes et que je vais souffrir.

sw.L: Na sasa, tazama, mimi nikiwa nimefungwa katika Roho, ninakwenda Yerusalemu, bila kujua mambo yatakayonikuta huko, \v 23 isipokuwa kwamba Roho Mtakatifu ananishuhudia kwa dhati katika kila mji, akisema kwamba vifungo na dhiki vinanisubiri.
sw.B: Na sasa, nikiwa nimefungwa na Roho, ninakwenda Yerusalemu. Sijui yatakayonipata huko, \v 23 isipokuwa kwamba katika mji mmoja baada ya mwingine Roho Mtakatifu ananishuhudia kwamba minyororo na mateso yananingoja.
sw.R: Sasa Roho Mtakatifu ananiongoza kwenda Yerusalemu, nami ni lazima niende. Sijui yatakayonipata huko. \v 23 Ninajua jambo hili tu: katika kila mji ninaoutembelea, Roho Mtakatifu ananiambia kwamba nitafungwa minyororo na kuteseka.

decisions.choice: bound in the Spirit: compelled by the Holy Spirit to go
alternatives: bound in my spirit: firmly resolved in his own mind
decisions.reason: The same phrase in 19:21 can mean either. In 20:23 and 21:4 it is the Holy Spirit who speaks about the journey, which favors the Holy Spirit here; but Paul's own resolve also fits.

decisions.choice: bound: under constraint; it also points ahead to the chains of 20:23
decisions.reason: He goes as one bound to obey, and he will soon be bound in fact (21:11, 21:33).

decisions.choice: in every city: in city after city along the way
decisions.reason: 21:4 and 21:10-11 show how the Spirit spoke through believers on the way.

decisions.choice: afflictions: troubles and distress
decisions.reason: The word is used of the pressures and persecutions believers suffer (14:22).

decisions.choice: the Holy Spirit is leading me, and I must go
decisions.reason: Readable follows the meaning chosen above and explains "bound".

decisions.choice: atado
decisions.reason: "Atado" keeps the picture of being bound, which points ahead to the chains ("cadenas") of 20:23 (meaning decision m2); Readable says plainly that the Spirit leads him, as the English Readable does.

source.text: ἀλλ’ οὐδενὸς λόγου ποιοῦμαι τὴν ψυχὴν τιμίαν ἐμαυτῷ ὡς τελειῶσαι τὸν δρόμον μου καὶ τὴν διακονίαν ἣν ἔλαβον παρὰ τοῦ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ, διαμαρτύρασθαι τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τῆς χάριτος τοῦ θεοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: But of nothing account I make the life precious to myself, so as to finish the course of me and the ministry which I received from the Lord Jesus, to testify solemnly the gospel of the grace of the God.

en.L: But I do not account my life of any value [as] precious to myself, so that I may finish my course and the ministry that I received from the Lord Jesus, to testify solemnly to the gospel of the grace of God.
en.B: But I set no value on my life, as if it were precious to me. All I want is to run my course to the end and carry out the ministry I received from the Lord Jesus: to bear full witness to the gospel of the grace of God.
en.R: But my life does not matter to me. What matters is that I finish the work the Lord Jesus gave me, like a runner who finishes the race. My work is to tell people the good news of God's grace, the kindness {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} shows to people who do not deserve it.

es.L: Pero no considero mi vida de ningún valor, [como] preciosa para mí mismo, con tal de terminar mi carrera y el servicio que recibí del Señor Jesús: dar testimonio solemne del evangelio de la gracia de Dios.
es.B: Pero no le doy ningún valor a mi vida, como si me fuera preciosa. Lo único que quiero es terminar mi carrera y cumplir el servicio que recibí del Señor Jesús: dar testimonio pleno del evangelio de la gracia de Dios.
es.R: Pero mi vida no me importa. Lo que importa es que yo termine el trabajo que me dio el Señor Jesús, como un corredor que termina la carrera. Mi trabajo es contarle a la gente la buena noticia de la gracia de Dios, la bondad que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} muestra a quienes no la merecen.

fr.L: Mais je ne fais aucun cas de ma vie, [comme si elle était] précieuse pour moi-même, pourvu que j’achève ma course et le ministère que j’ai reçu du Seigneur Jésus : rendre pleinement témoignage à l’Évangile de la grâce de Dieu.
fr.B: Mais je n’accorde aucune valeur à ma vie, comme si elle m’était précieuse. Tout ce que je veux, c’est mener ma course jusqu’au bout et accomplir le ministère que j’ai reçu du Seigneur Jésus : rendre un témoignage complet à l’Évangile de la grâce de Dieu.
fr.R: Mais ma vie n’a pas d’importance pour moi. Ce qui compte, c’est que je termine le travail que le Seigneur Jésus m’a donné, comme un coureur qui termine la course. Mon travail, c’est d’annoncer aux gens la bonne nouvelle de la grâce de Dieu, la bonté qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} montre à ceux qui ne la méritent pas.

sw.L: Lakini siyahesabu maisha yangu kuwa na thamani yoyote kwangu mwenyewe, ili nimalize mbio zangu na huduma niliyopokea kutoka kwa Bwana Yesu, kuishuhudia kwa dhati Injili ya neema ya Mungu.
sw.B: Lakini sioni maisha yangu kuwa na thamani yoyote, kana kwamba ni ya thamani kwangu. Ninachotaka tu ni kumaliza mbio zangu na kukamilisha huduma niliyopokea kutoka kwa Bwana Yesu: kuishuhudia kikamilifu Injili ya neema ya Mungu.
sw.R: Lakini maisha yangu si kitu kwangu. Kilicho muhimu ni kwamba nimalize kazi ambayo Bwana Yesu alinipa, kama mkimbiaji anayemaliza mbio zake. Kazi yangu ni kuwaambia watu habari njema ya neema ya Mungu, yaani wema {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} anaowaonyesha watu wasiostahili.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: the shorter reading
alternatives: many later manuscripts read "But I make account of none of these things, nor do I count my life precious to myself"
many manuscripts add "with joy" after "my course"
decisions.reason: The early manuscripts have the shorter, harder wording; the fuller forms smooth it out. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: he counts his life worth nothing, compared with finishing his task
decisions.reason: The compressed Greek says that his own life is not what he holds dear; his aim is to complete what the Lord gave him.

decisions.choice: my course: the race a runner must finish
decisions.reason: Paul uses the picture of a race for his work (1 Corinthians 9:24; 2 Timothy 4:7).

decisions.choice: the gospel of the grace of God: the good news that God gives his favor freely
decisions.reason: Grace is God's undeserved kindness (15:11, 20:32).

decisions.choice: like a runner who finishes the race; the kindness he shows to people who do not deserve it
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture and the word grace, and keeps the word.

decisions.choice: el servicio
decisions.reason: The Greek word is the ordinary word for service, from the same root as "servir" in the term sheet; "ministerio" now suggests a church office or a government department.

decisions.choice: l’Évangile (L, B); la bonne nouvelle (R)
alternatives: la bonne nouvelle at every level
decisions.reason: As the term sheet settles for the New Testament.

source.text: Καὶ νῦν ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ οἶδα ὅτι οὐκέτι ὄψεσθε τὸ πρόσωπόν μου ὑμεῖς πάντες ἐν οἷς διῆλθον κηρύσσων τὴν βασιλείαν.

records.literal_gloss: And now behold I know that no longer will see the face of me you all among whom I went about proclaiming the kingdom.

en.L: And now, look, I know that you all, among whom I went about proclaiming the kingdom, will no longer see my face.
en.B: And now I know this: you will not see my face again, not one of you among whom I have gone from place to place proclaiming the kingdom.
en.R: Now I know that none of you will see me again. I traveled among you and told you about God's kingdom, but you will not see me again.

es.L: Y ahora, {{plural_you:miren|mirad}}, yo sé que ya no {{plural_you:verán|veréis}} mi rostro {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} todos, entre quienes pasé proclamando el reino.
es.B: Y ahora sé esto: ninguno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, entre quienes he andado de lugar en lugar proclamando el reino, volverá a ver mi rostro.
es.R: Ahora sé que ninguno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} me volverá a ver. Anduve entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} y {{plural_you:les|os}} hablé del reino de Dios, pero no me {{plural_you:volverán|volveréis}} a ver.

fr.L: Et maintenant, voici, je sais que vous ne verrez plus mon visage, vous tous parmi lesquels je suis passé en proclamant le royaume.
fr.B: Et maintenant, je le sais : vous ne reverrez plus mon visage, aucun de vous, parmi lesquels je suis allé de lieu en lieu proclamer le royaume.
fr.R: Maintenant, je sais qu’aucun de vous ne me reverra. Je suis passé chez vous et je vous ai parlé du royaume de Dieu, mais vous ne me reverrez plus.

sw.L: Na sasa, tazama, mimi najua kwamba ninyi nyote, ambao nilipita kati yenu nikihubiri ufalme, hamtauona tena uso wangu.
sw.B: Na sasa ninajua hili: hamtauona uso wangu tena, hata mmoja wenu ambao nimezunguka kati yenu nikihubiri ufalme.
sw.R: Sasa ninajua kwamba hakuna hata mmoja wenu atakayeniona tena. Nilisafiri kati yenu na kuwaambia habari za ufalme wa Mungu, lakini hamtaniona tena.

decisions.choice: I know: Paul's firm conviction
decisions.reason: He does not say how he knows. The Spirit has warned him of chains (20:23), but not in these words.

decisions.choice: the kingdom: God's reign, which Paul proclaimed
decisions.reason: As in 19:8 and 28:31, where Paul proclaims the kingdom of God.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "the kingdom"
alternatives: some manuscripts read "the kingdom of God" or "the kingdom of Jesus"
decisions.reason: The short reading is in early manuscripts; the additions say whose kingdom it is. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: God's kingdom
decisions.reason: Readable says whose kingdom, as 19:8 does.

source.text: διότι μαρτύρομαι ὑμῖν ἐν τῇ σήμερον ἡμέρᾳ ὅτι καθαρός εἰμι ἀπὸ τοῦ αἵματος πάντων, οὐ γὰρ ὑπεστειλάμην τοῦ μὴ ἀναγγεῖλαι πᾶσαν τὴν βουλὴν τοῦ θεοῦ ὑμῖν.

records.literal_gloss: Therefore I testify to you on the today day that clean I am from the blood of all; \v 27 not for I held back of the not to declare all the counsel of the God to you.

en.L: Therefore I testify to you on this very day that I am clean from the blood of all, \v 27 for I did not hold back from declaring to you the whole counsel of God.
en.B: So on this day I solemnly tell you: I am free from guilt for anyone's blood. \v 27 I never drew back from making known to you God's whole plan.
en.R: So today I tell you this: if any of you are lost, it is not my fault. \v 27 I told you everything God wants you to know about {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} plan.

es.L: Por tanto, {{plural_you:les|os}} testifico en el día de hoy que estoy limpio de la sangre de todos, \v 27 porque no me retraje de {{plural_you:anunciarles|anunciaros}} todo el consejo de Dios.
es.B: Por eso, en este día {{plural_you:les|os}} declaro solemnemente que no soy culpable de la sangre de nadie. \v 27 Nunca me eché atrás a la hora de {{plural_you:darles|daros}} a conocer todo el plan de Dios.
es.R: Por eso hoy {{plural_you:les|os}} digo esto: si alguno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} se pierde, no será culpa mía. \v 27 {{plural_you:Les|Os}} dije todo lo que Dios quiere que {{plural_you:sepan|sepáis}} acerca de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} plan.

fr.L: C’est pourquoi je vous atteste en ce jour même que je suis pur du sang de tous, \v 27 car je ne me suis pas retenu de vous annoncer tout le dessein de Dieu.
fr.B: Aussi je vous le déclare solennellement aujourd’hui : je suis innocent du sang de qui que ce soit. \v 27 Je n’ai jamais renoncé à vous faire connaître tout le plan de Dieu.
fr.R: Alors aujourd’hui, je vous dis ceci : si l’un de vous est perdu, ce n’est pas ma faute. \v 27 Je vous ai dit tout ce que Dieu veut que vous sachiez de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} plan.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo nawashuhudia leo hii kwamba mimi ni safi, sina [hatia ya] damu ya watu wote; \v 27 kwa maana sikujizuia kuwatangazia shauri lote la Mungu.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo leo hii nawaambia kwa dhati: sina hatia ya damu ya mtu yeyote. \v 27 Sikurudi nyuma kuwajulisha mpango wote wa Mungu.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo leo nawaambia hivi: kama yeyote kati yenu atapotea, si kosa langu. \v 27 Niliwaambia kila kitu ambacho Mungu anataka mjue kuhusu mpango {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.

decisions.choice: clean from the blood of all: free from guilt, like the watchman who gave warning
decisions.reason: In Ezekiel 3:18-21 and 33:1-9 the watchman who warns the people is not guilty of their blood. Paul used the same picture in 18:6.

decisions.choice: counsel: God's purpose and plan
decisions.reason: As in 2:23, 4:28 and 13:36, the word is used of what God has willed and planned.

decisions.choice: this day: this last meeting
decisions.reason: Paul speaks as one who will not see them again (20:25).

decisions.choice: if any of you are lost, it is not my fault
alternatives: I am clean from the blood of all
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture, following the meaning note.

source.text: προσέχετε ἑαυτοῖς καὶ παντὶ τῷ ποιμνίῳ, ἐν ᾧ ὑμᾶς τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον ἔθετο ἐπισκόπους, ποιμαίνειν τὴν ἐκκλησίαν τοῦ θεοῦ, ἣν περιεποιήσατο διὰ τοῦ αἵματος τοῦ ἰδίου.

records.literal_gloss: Take heed to yourselves and to all the flock, in which you the Spirit the Holy has placed overseers, to shepherd the church of the God, which he acquired through the blood of the own.

en.L: Take heed to yourselves and to all the flock, among which the Holy Spirit has made you overseers, to shepherd the church of God, which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} acquired through {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own blood.
en.B: Be on your guard, for yourselves and for the whole flock, in which the Holy Spirit has made you overseers to shepherd the church of God, which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} won for {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} through {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own blood.
en.R: Be careful how you live, and watch over all the believers, who are like a flock of sheep. The Holy Spirit has put you in charge of them as overseers. Care for God's church as a shepherd cares for sheep. God paid for it with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own blood.

es.L: {{plural_you:Tengan|Tened}} cuidado de {{plural_you:ustedes mismos|vosotros mismos}} y de todo el rebaño, en el cual el Espíritu Santo {{plural_you:los|os}} ha puesto [como] supervisores, para pastorear la iglesia de Dios, que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} adquirió por medio de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} propia sangre.
es.B: {{plural_you:Estén|Estad}} en guardia, por {{plural_you:ustedes mismos|vosotros mismos}} y por todo el rebaño, en el que el Espíritu Santo {{plural_you:los|os}} ha puesto como supervisores para pastorear la iglesia de Dios, que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} ganó para {{deity_pronoun:sí mismo|Sí mismo}} con {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} propia sangre.
es.R: {{plural_you:Tengan|Tened}} cuidado de cómo {{plural_you:viven|vivís}}, y {{plural_you:vigilen|vigilad}} a todos los creyentes, que son como un rebaño de ovejas. El Espíritu Santo {{plural_you:los|os}} ha puesto a cargo de ellos como líderes de la iglesia. {{plural_you:Cuiden|Cuidad}} la iglesia de Dios como un pastor cuida a sus ovejas. Dios pagó por ella con {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} propia sangre.

fr.L: Prenez garde à vous-mêmes et à tout le troupeau, dans lequel l’Esprit Saint vous a établis surveillants, pour paître l’Église de Dieu, qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a acquise par {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} propre sang.
fr.B: Veillez sur vous-mêmes et sur tout le troupeau dont l’Esprit Saint vous a établis surveillants, pour être les bergers de l’Église de Dieu, qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a gagnée pour {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} par {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} propre sang.
fr.R: Faites attention à votre manière de vivre, et veillez sur tous les croyants, qui sont comme un troupeau de moutons. L’Esprit Saint vous a placés à leur tête comme responsables. Prenez soin de l’Église de Dieu comme un berger prend soin de ses moutons. Dieu l’a payée de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} propre sang.
